tldr: Tuesday pulled back from Monday's violent Nvidia-CEO-reinstatement snapback (S&P -0.50% to 7201.09, Nasdaq -1.48%, VIX 26.36), and new research this run shows Monday's +4.73% rally was hedge-fund short-covering (Goldman desk conviction only 5/10), not fresh institutional buying -- a shaky foundation for further upside.

The Fed regime flipped hawkish into a growth scare: Dec-9 hike odds now ~93-96% (not a cut) as core CPI hit a six-month high 2.8% y/y even as core PCE cooled to 2.2% -- tonight's Core PCE + GDP (21:30 SGT) are the last clean reads before the FOMC.

Silver and gold miners gave back more of Monday's bounce (SLV -5.32% to $36.84, GDX -1.96%, GLD -2.27%); silver is now ~65% below its January peak with the gold-silver ratio blown out to ~86 -- the book's largest single risk leg is still live and falling.

Asia diverged a session behind the US: Korea's 7-session foreign-selling streak broke on a +6.32% KOSPI catch-up rally (retail sold into it for once), while Hong Kong's Southbound flow flipped back to buying (+HK$6.2bn) even as the HSI itself closed red.
Credit still refuses to confirm the equity bounce: HY OAS ~352-376bp, CCC spreads ~1,135-1,350bp (+49% YTD), with Nvidia-linked CoreWeave debt trading at distressed levels.

Smart money split on AI: Berkshire held its $30.1B Alphabet stake completely unchanged through the crash while ARK dumped ~$134M of Broadcom on the crash day; Congress logged a fresh NVDA buy (Rep. Salazar) and a lame-duck member (Kean) rotating out of equities into a Treasury note.

Macro regime reframed from 'mechanical snapback' to a hawkish-Fed stagflation crosscurrent; all 40 model calls plus a 9-name rare-earth basket (added NEO.TO, ILU.AX, 6680.HK) re-levelled against the new Dec-hike pricing and the short-covering finding.

Market sentiment: Fear&Greed held at 17/Extreme Fear (re-confirmed via 3 independent CNN-methodology reconstructions); breadth confirmed narrow -- only 3-of-11 S&P sectors above their 200-DMA despite Monday's rally.

Flows: global EPFR/BofA/Lipper still week-ending-18-Nov (unchanged, next due ~27 Nov); Korea and Hong Kong both added genuinely newer Nov-24 daily prints; new US color shows Monday's rally was short-covering, not institutional buying.
News: 13 fresh items, 8 from the last 24-48h (credit-spread blowout, silver crash continuation, Nvidia SEC-probe detail, Korea/HK catch-up rallies).
Investors: Trump profile checked against Forbes/OGE -- no material change since 17 Nov, left as-is; DJT/WLFI/TRUMP-coin weakness is a continuation already in the existing note.

regime.label: Hawkish-Fed stagflation crosscurrent inside an unresolved AI-capex/credit-stress regime
regime.oneLiner: The Fed is now pricing a December hike, not a cut, directly into an unresolved AI-capex growth scare, and Monday's rally turns out to have been short-covering rather than conviction buying.
